source: National Archives Bill of Rights transcript, Amendment IV
review_notes: Codex reviewed the complete Fourth Amendment sentence. The four protected interests and two kinds of unreasonable intrusion yield eight rights, each with a separate nonviolation rule. The warrant clause adds a probable-cause requirement, oath or affirmation support for that cause, and three description targets. Coordination is expanded without asserting that any actual search, seizure, or warrant occurred. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
Amendment IV

The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no Warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the persons or things to be seized.
